usage.outputShape: Raw binary PDF (application/pdf); paid_fetch returns it as a base64-prefixed string ('base64:...'). Response headers include x-pages (page count) and content-disposition with the filename derived from options.title.
quirks: Response body is a raw binary PDF, not JSON. paid_fetch surfaces it as a 'base64:...' string — strip the prefix and decode to get the PDF bytes.

The service has two endpoints: /api/v1/markdown ($0.01, GFM input) and /api/v1/render ($0.02, template/DSL input). Use markdown for simple docs; use render with a templateId from GET /api/v1/templates?owner=library for branded layouts.
options.title sets the content-disposition filename. x-pages and x-render-ms headers report page count and render latency.
usage.guide: POST GitHub-Flavoured Markdown to /api/v1/markdown with optional options object (title, pageSize, fontFamily, fontSize, margins, theme). Payment of $0.01 USDC on Base is handled automatically via x402. The response is a binary PDF returned synchronously — paid_fetch delivers it as a base64-prefixed string; strip the 'base64:' prefix and decode to obtain the raw bytes. For template-based generation (PDF/UA-1 + PDF/A-2A compliant), use /api/v1/render at $0.02 with a templateId from GET /api/v1/templates?owner=library and a data object supplying placeholder values.
